reforms.description: The federal government has committed CAD 360 million over three years to engage with Indigenous Peoples to develop an Indigenous Early Learning and Child Care Framework, aiming to improve educational outcomes for Indigenous children.
reforms.package_name: Indigenous Early Learning and Child Care Framework
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investing in early childhood education for Indigenous children is expected to enhance their educational outcomes, which can lead to better employment opportunities and economic participation in the long run.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has committed funding to develop the framework.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative represents a significant investment in human capital aimed at addressing educational disparities among Indigenous populations, which is crucial for long-term economic growth.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government has committed CAD 360 million over three years to engage with Indigenous Peoples to develop an Indigenous Early Learning and Child Care Framework.

reforms.description: The Canadian government allocated CAD 400 million over three years for the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative to increase late-stage financing available to Canadian entrepreneurs.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increases access to late-stage financing, which is crucial for scaling innovative startups and enhancing their contribution to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The funding has been allocated to support late-stage financing for entrepreneurs.
reforms.importance_rationale: This funding represents a significant investment in the venture capital landscape, aimed at addressing a critical gap in financing for innovative firms.
reforms.source_quote: A positive step in this regard is the CAD 400 million funding over three years for the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative, which will increase late-stage financing available to Canadian entrepreneurs.

reforms.description: The federal government allocated CAD 950 million to accelerate innovation through five regional 'superclusters', which aims to boost economic growth by leveraging existing local strengths.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By fostering collaboration and innovation in key regional sectors, this initiative is expected to enhance productivity and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has allocated CAD 950 million to accelerate innovation through five regional 'superclusters'.
reforms.importance_rationale: This funding is a significant investment aimed at enhancing regional innovation ecosystems, which can lead to substantial economic benefits.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government has also allocated CAD 950 million to accelerate innovation through five regional 'superclusters', which has the potential to boost economic growth through one-off funding that complements existing local strengths.

reforms.description: The 2018 federal budget included around CAD 650 million per year in additional funding for research and development, focusing on fundamental research where market failures are most prevalent.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased funding for fundamental research addresses critical market failures and supports long-term innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2018 federal budget allocated additional funding for research and development.
reforms.importance_rationale: This funding is a significant enhancement to the public R&D budget, aimed at strengthening Canada's research capabilities.
reforms.source_quote: Around CAD 650 million per year in additional funding for research and development in the 2018 federal budget is focussed on fundamental research, where market failures are most pervasive.

reforms.description: The Government of Canada will be collecting better data to evaluate interventions in a robust manner, with new funding for this purpose provided in Budget 2018 to Statistics Canada and the Treasury Board Secretariat.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improved data collection will enhance the evaluation of innovation programs, leading to more effective policy decisions and resource allocation.
reforms.status_evidence: New funding for data collection was provided in Budget 2018.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative represents a significant step towards enhancing the effectiveness of innovation programs through better evaluation mechanisms.
reforms.source_quote: As an outcome of the 2017 horizontal review of federal business innovation programmes, the Government of Canada will be collecting better data to be able to evaluate interventions in a robust manner, with new funding for this purpose provided in Budget 2018 to Statistics Canada and the Treasury Board Secretariat.

reforms.description: Budget 2017 provided CAD 221 million over five years to provide work experience in businesses to Canadian post-secondary students, generally at the graduate-level, through the Student Work Placements programme.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: This funding enhances the skills and employability of students, fostering a more skilled workforce that can contribute to innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Funding is delivered by Mitacs, a not-for-profit organisation that builds partnerships between industry and educational institutions.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative significantly increases opportunities for students to gain practical experience, which is crucial for enhancing their employability and skills relevant to the innovation sector.
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2017 provided CAD 221 million over five years, starting in 2017–18, to provide work experience in businesses to Canadian post-secondary students, generally at the graduate-level.

reforms.description: BDC has committed to investing CAD 200 million in women-led technology firms over 2018-19 to 2022-23.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: This investment aims to enhance the growth of women-led technology firms, contributing to diversity in the startup ecosystem and fostering innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: BDC has committed to investing CAD 200 million in women-led technology firms.
reforms.importance_rationale: This commitment represents a significant investment aimed at supporting underrepresented groups in the technology sector, which is crucial for fostering a more inclusive innovation landscape.
reforms.source_quote: BDC has committed to investing CAD 200 million in women-led technology firms over 2018-19 to 2022-23.

reforms.description: The federal government has prioritized supporting women entrepreneurs through the Women Entrepreneurship Strategy, which includes CAD 1.4 billion in new financing and aims to narrow entrepreneurship gaps.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By increasing access to financing for women entrepreneurs, the strategy aims to enhance economic participation and productivity, which can lead to overall economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has given priority to supporting women entrepreneurs through the Women Entrepreneurship Strategy.
reforms.importance_rationale: This strategy represents a significant structural change aimed at addressing gender disparities in entrepreneurship, which is crucial for economic inclusivity and growth.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government has given priority to supporting women entrepreneurs through the Women Entrepreneurship Strategy, which has the potential to bring together scattered existing programmes and build institutional consensus on the policies required to narrow entrepreneurship gaps.

reforms.description: The government provided additional funding in its 2018 Budget to support doubling the number of job placements funded under the Canada Summer Jobs program, which aims to enhance youth employment opportunities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By increasing job placements, the initiative enhances youth employability and aligns workforce skills with business needs, contributing to overall economic productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The government provided additional funding to support the program.
reforms.importance_rationale: The expansion of the Canada Summer Jobs program represents a significant investment in youth employment, addressing immediate labor market needs and enhancing skills development.
reforms.source_quote: The government provided additional funding in its 2018 Budget to support doubling of the number of job placements funded under the Canada Summer Jobs program.

reforms.description: The Student Work-Integrated Learning Program was launched to help post-secondary students in STEM and business programs gain work experience, thereby enhancing their employability.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: This program aims to bridge the gap between education and employment, equipping students with practical skills that are in demand in the labor market.
reforms.status_evidence: The program was launched to assist students in gaining work experience.
reforms.importance_rationale: The program represents a targeted effort to improve the employability of students in key sectors, addressing skills mismatches in the labor market.
reforms.source_quote: The government launched the Student Work-Integrated Learning Program to help post-secondary students in STEM and business programs get work experience.

reforms.description: A new Pre-Apprenticeship Program was announced in the 2018 federal Budget to target underrepresented groups in the trades, including women, youth, Indigenous Peoples, and new immigrants.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By targeting underrepresented groups, the program aims to enhance diversity in the trades and improve overall labor market participation, which can lead to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The Pre-Apprenticeship Program was announced to support underrepresented groups in the trades.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative is significant in promoting inclusivity in the trades, addressing labor shortages, and enhancing the skill set of the workforce.
reforms.source_quote: A new Pre-Apprenticeship Program announced in the 2018 federal Budget will target people who are currently underrepresented in the trades.

reforms.description: A major change occurred in 2002, when the points-based system for selecting economic-class immigrants was overhauled to focus on human capital factors, such as educational attainment and language ability, rather than short-term labour market shortages.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By selecting immigrants based on long-term economic needs and human capital, the reform aims to enhance the productivity and skills of the workforce, contributing positively to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The points-based system was overhauled as part of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a structural change in immigration policy, significantly altering how immigrants are selected based on their potential economic contributions, which has long-term implications for the labor market.
reforms.source_quote: A major change occurred in 2002, when the points-based system was overhauled.

reforms.description: The Targeted Employment Strategy for Newcomers aims to facilitate foreign-credentials recognition and help immigrants gain Canadian work experience in their profession through improved pre-arrival supports and targeted employment-assistance measures.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By improving the recognition of foreign credentials and providing work experience, the strategy enhances the employability of newcomers, thereby increasing productivity and economic contribution.
reforms.status_evidence: The strategy includes several pilots underway to gather evidence on effective approaches.
reforms.importance_rationale: The strategy addresses a significant barrier to employment for newcomers, which is the recognition of foreign credentials, and aims to improve their integration into the labor market.
reforms.source_quote: The Targeted Employment Strategy for Newcomers announced in the 2017 budget is aimed at facilitating foreign-credentials recognition and helping immigrants to gain Canadian work experience in their profession.

reforms.description: The creation of Offices of the Fairness Commissioner in various provinces aims to ensure that registration practices in regulated professions are transparent and fair, helping to reduce barriers for immigrants seeking to practice their professions.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By streamlining registration processes and improving support for internationally trained professionals, the initiative enhances labor market participation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The Ontario OFC has guided changes that removed unnecessary hurdles for applicants through streamlined processes.
reforms.importance_rationale: The establishment of these offices represents a significant step towards improving the integration of skilled immigrants into the workforce by addressing regulatory barriers.
reforms.source_quote: A useful innovation to reduce unwarranted barriers to immigrants registering in licenced professions has been the creation of several Offices of the Fairness Commissioner (OFCs) in various provinces, starting with Ontario in 2006.
